title: Observability Onboarding Sprint Kit — Probe Prioritization
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact onboarding sprint kit for new operators and infra engineers joining the Observability squad. Focus: define a small, high-impact set of probes/metrics and a tracing annotation standard that lets on-callers diagnose token-path latency and tenant cold-cache problems quickly.

Audience:
- Observability engineers onboarding to inference telemetry
- SREs/ops oncall who will run postmortems for token-latency incidents
- Feature owners who need to add minimally invasive instrumentation to rollouts

High-level goals:
1) Ship 6 lightweight probes usable within 2 sprints.
2) Establish a trace attribute contract for token-serving calls.
3) Provide a single compact dashboard template (investigation-first) plus a cost panel.
4) Prioritize probes by impact/cost matrix so we focus instrument effort where it most reduces MTTI.

Glossary / metric definitions (short):
- token_latency_ms: per-response distribution; record per-request end-to-end time from API ingress to final token sent. Derive p50/p90/p95/p99.
- kv_cache_hit_ratio: fraction of requests where KV cache returned a valid prefix chunk (boolean per segment). Aim to tag by tenant+model.
- prefix_warmth_index: rolling percent of requests within last 10m that found a warm prefix (0-1). Useful for cold-cache tail analysis.
- batching_effective_size: mean tokens-per-batch measured at serving runtime (excludes empty padding).
- model_fanout_ratio: number of model forks or variants invoked per request (e.g., rerankers, fallback models).
- rerank_latency_ms: time spent in synchronous reranking pipelines; treat separately from LM generation latency.
- operator_action_rate: human-invoked mitigation actions (scale-ups, fallbacks) per hour — helps correlate to incidents.

Trace annotation contract (span/attribute guidance):
- Top-level request span: name = "request:ingress" attributes: {"tenant_id", "route", "request_id", "arrival_ts", "client_hint_seq_len"}.
- Token-gen span: name = "model:generate" attributes: {"model_name", "model_version", "hf_id?", "seq_length", "batch_id", "kv_cache_hit": "true/false", "quant_mode"}.
- Cache span: name = "kvcache:lookup" attributes: {"cache_key_shard", "lookup_latency_ms", "hit"}.
- Batcher span: name = "runtime:batch_assemble" attributes: {"effective_batch_size", "queued_ms"}.
- Fallback span: name = "fallback:invoke" attributes: {"fallback_reason", "fallback_model", "latency_ms"}.
- Annotation conventions: all span attributes are snake_case. tenant_id should be hashed in traces for privacy; include tenant_tier label where available. session_id for session-affinity flows must be propagated as "session_id" on top-level spans.

Sampling policy (practical):
- Full-trace sampling for: requests where token_latency_ms > p99 baseline OR kv_cache_hit=false AND request_size > threshold.
- 1% baseline sampling across traffic to capture distribution shapes.
- Adaptive burst sampling: if error_rate > 0.5% for a route, bump sampling to 10% for that route for next 30m.

Minimal investigation dashboard (layout notes):
Panel 1 — Quick triage row (single-line): p95 token_latency, request_rate, error_rate, kv_cache_hit_ratio (global + route filter).
Panel 2 — Session heatmap: prefix_warmth_index by tenant cohort over last 1h (rows=tenant_cohort, cols=5m bins).
Panel 3 — Trace anchor links: top contributing spans to latency (group by span name, show avg latency & 95th). Provide direct trace links for top 5 slow sessions.
Panel 4 — Batch effectiveness: effective_batch_size distribution and queued_ms percentiles.
Panel 5 — Cost & capacity: model_fanout_ratio, GPU_utilization_by_pool, token_tokens_generated_count (token volumes).
Panel 6 — Operator cues: operator_action_rate and last 6 manual actions with short notes.
Notes on dashboard behavior: default filters should be last 30m, tenant=all, model=all. Provide drop-down to pin route/model/tenant. Make the Troubleshooting column narrow so operators can get to traces quickly.

Probe prioritization matrix (text matrix):
- Axis: impact on MTTI (High/Med/Low) vs instrument cost (High/Med/Low).
- High impact / Low cost (priority A): kv_cache_hit_ratio (per-tenant), token_latency_ms p95 for cold starts, batch_size distribution.
- High impact / Med cost (priority B): full-trace sampling for cold-cache tail, model_fanout_ratio per-route.
- Med impact / Low cost (priority C): rerank_latency_ms, operator_action_rate logging.
- Low impact / High cost (defer): per-token attention matrix dumps, deep kernel-level microtimers unless investigating specific hardware regressions.

Sprint tasks (first two-week sprint):
1) Instrument kv_cache_hit_ratio tag on cache lookup code (owner: Priya). Deliverable: metric + basic dashboard tile.
2) Add token_latency_ms timers at ingress and model return (owner: Avery). Deliverable: p50/p90/p95 panels + alert rule for p99 > threshold.
3) Implement trace attribute propagation for batch_id and session_id (owner: Diego). Deliverable: sample traces for 10k requests.
4) Small dashboard template check-in — wiring up panels 1–4 using templated variables (owner: Sofia).
5) Add a canary sampling toggle reachable from Console to bump sampling for routes (owner: Priya).

Alerting and SLO notes (starter guidance):
- SLO candidate: request_success_rate >= 99.9% (1m window for paging alerts; 1h window for SLO burn).
- Latency SLO: p95 token_latency_ms <= X ms (X to be determined per-model class; baseline with recent production run).
- Alert rule suggestion: if kv_cache_hit_ratio drops > 20% vs baseline AND p95 latency increases by > 30% -> paging to oncall.

Investigation playbook (short runbook):
1) Open the investigation-first dashboard, set time to last 60m.
2) Filter to affected route/tenant, look at Panel 1 for p95 spike and kv cache change.
3) Jump to trace anchor list; find top slow trace(s) and inspect model:generate spans for kv_cache_hit and batch_id.
4) If batch queued_ms is high -> correlate with autoscaler and GPU_utilization_by_pool.
5) If kv_cache_hit=false for many requests -> check prefix_warmth_index and recent model rollouts (linked PR).
6) Create ticket with trace links + minimal repro prompt and assign to oncall rotation.

Example query snippets (pseudocode to adapt to metrics store):
- kv cache hit ratio (series): SELECT sum(if(hit,1,0))/count(*) FROM kvcache_lookup WHERE tenant_hash = "$tenant" AND window = 5m
- token latency p95: SELECT percentile(token_latency_ms,95) FROM tokens_by_request WHERE route="$route" AND window=5m
- batch size distribution: SELECT histogram(effective_batch_size) FROM runtime_batch_assemble WHERE pool="$pool"

Privacy & data controls:
- Strip/never log raw prompt text to traces except for internal dev-sandbox routes. Store only prompt length and a hashed prompt fingerprint if needed.
- Tenant identifiers in traces must be hashed; store tenant_tier as cleartext for prioritization.

Owner responsibilities & handoff notes:
- Onboarding owners are expected to run a 30-minute walkthrough for new hires using this kit.
- Owners should update the linked confluence page and attach a screenshot of the dashboard after the first production incident response.

Open questions / backlog:
- Decide p95 latency thresholds per model class (small/medium/large).
- Where to place persisted prefix_warmth history (TSDB vs short-term cache) — impacts query cost.
- Finalize sampling quotas by tenant tier to balance privacy and investigatability.

Next steps (immediate):
- Kickoff meeting with infra + serving-runtime on 2025-01-20 (owner: Avery).
- Ship kv_cache_hit_ratio metric by 2025-01-31.
- Create PR template for trace attribute changes (owner: Diego).
